claims.statement: Code is grouped by domain (DDD-influenced layout, TES-68) into four layers: app/ thin routes, modules/<domain>/{data,domain,ui} one module per PRD FR (14 domains), shared/ leaf level, and lib/supabase/ as the external data boundary; new code goes inside its owning module, not new top-level folders.

No business logic lives in app/: Server Components fetch via a module's data/ layer and compose module UI over shared/ui primitives (review-level rule), as exemplified by the dashboard and billing pages importing data/, domain/, and ui/ surfaces of multiple modules.
The import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is ESLint-enforced via import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs covering the app/, modules/, shared/, and lib/ trees.

Another module's data/ is private to every other module: its public surface is domain/ + ui/, and only app/ may fetch from any module's data/; the lint zones are generated per domain from the 14-entry domains array in eslint.config.mjs.

shared/ is the leaf level and must never import modules/ or app/ (lint-enforced); it contains the single-file shared/types.ts UI domain types, props-only shared/ui/ primitives (a shared/ui component that reads data or encodes business rules moves to its owning module), shared/vocab.ts fixed TESDA terms (EGACE_STAGES, EMPLOYMENT_STATUSES), and shared/text.ts copy shaping — shared/mocks/ was removed entirely in the mock-data retirement.

Only module data/ layers (besides lib/supabase itself) may import lib/supabase/database.types.ts; app/, shared/, and modules' ui/ and domain/ are lint-blocked from raw DB row types and must import domain types instead.

Two type families stay deliberately separate: the generated lib/supabase/database.types.ts (raw rows with Row/Insert/Update per table plus seven Postgres enums) and hand-written shared/types.ts (UI domain types, with Batch as a hub type referencing six other domains); the mappers in module data/ layers are the only seam between them.

Every entity contract follows fetch → map → derive per the reference implementation modules/batches/data/batches.ts: fetch is a typed Supabase query whose rows are scoped by RLS (never manually filtered by tenant in JS), map is a pure DB-row to domain translation, derive computes lifecycle/date helpers.

mapBatchRow is pure (no I/O), exported for unit tests, and marks schema gaps with TODO(contract) defaults so the UI shape stays valid — e.g. billingDeadline and daysToBilling stand in on end_date because no billing_deadline column exists yet.

Data functions return discriminated snapshots with a core trio: ok (mapped rows plus dataAsOf = freshest updated_at, authoritative even when empty), sync-failed (Supabase configured but the query errored or the client threw — must surface a sync-failed banner), and unconfigured (isSupabaseConfigured() is false); neither unconfigured nor sync-failed may substitute mock or fabricated data — both render an honest empty state, the old shared/mocks fallback having been retired.

Modules extend the snapshot trio with genuinely distinct states: tenancy's ProfileSnapshot adds not-found (user authenticated via Clerk but no profiles row yet — webhook racing or failed, 'no access yet' rather than an error), and import's LearnerImportSnapshot adds validation-failed (CSV structurally invalid, checked before any Supabase client is created).

Raw error strings never reach the UI: the sync-failed snapshot traps the error server-side and the dashboard renders fixed copy — 'Sync with Supabase failed — showing the last cached snapshot' (or '…the currently loaded data' when a ?state= preview override flags failure while the real snapshot is ok), with a ' from <timestamp>' data-as-of label or nothing appended plus a Retry link — while a zero-row failure renders the fixed 'Couldn't reach Supabase' view; RULES 1.6 forbids leaking raw Supabase/SQL errors, table names, or internal IDs.

DB_TO_UI_STAGE in modules/batches/data/batches.ts is a total (non-Partial) enum-bridge map so a new DB enum variant fails compilation until its UI treatment is chosen: training/assessment/billing map to UI train/assess/bill, entre is UI-only with no DB column, completed/blocked map to null and are special-cased by deriveLifecycle (all stages done / no stage active), and normalizeStatus surfaces DB blocked as UI pending.

The total-map bridge convention repeats across data layers — STAGE_TO_UI (documents), ACTION_TO_TONE (activity), DB_TO_UI_ROLE (tenancy, DB role a strict subset of UI roles), ASSESSMENT_RESULT_TO_UI (learners) — while DOCUMENT_ICONS is deliberately a Partial map because document_key is per-program configured data, not a closed enum.

Because a module's data/ is private, batches.ts hand-duplicates documents.ts's mapper logic (MISSING_DOC, mapDocumentRow, the catalog backfill in mapDocumentsMap/mapDocumentRows), kept in sync by hand rather than imported; activity.ts's toRelativeWhen mirrors batches.ts's toDisplayDate with the same unparseable-date-to-empty-string convention.

Cross-module data needs are satisfied by pass-by-parameter or by importing the other module's public domain/: tenancy's getProfileSnapshot(clerkUserId) takes the caller's Clerk user id as a parameter because resolving it is auth/data's private job (app/ wires the two data/ layers together), and data layers import other modules' domain/ — modules/batches/data/metrics.ts and modules/billing/data/billing.ts both import modules/documents/domain/compliance, with billing/data fully derive-only and free of any shared/mocks dependency.

domain/ layers are pure business rules with no I/O (e.g. urgencyTier in modules/batches/domain/urgency.ts) and are unit-tested with fixed as-of dates; shared/ must not re-export module code — domain logic that lived in the retired mock facade (urgency, billing readiness, dashboard metrics) now lives in module domain/ layers.

The per-module split of shared/types.ts was deliberately deferred (TES-68) while shared/mocks/seed.ts constructed 11 of these domain types — shared/ can never import modules/, so moving the types into modules would have broken the import boundary — but the mock-data retirement removed that blocker: RULES 2.16 is struck through as resolved and the split is now unblocked; shared/types.ts remains a single file, with Batch's hub role (referencing six other domains) as the practical cost of splitting.

lib/supabase/ is the external data boundary: server.ts builds an anon-key client and attaches the caller's Clerk session token via the accessToken callback, throwing (NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE) when no token exists instead of silently querying as anon (which RLS would answer with zero rows and no error); service.ts holds the RLS-bypassing service-role client reserved for server-to-server webhook provisioning only.
No index barrels exist anywhere — deep imports are the convention (shared/README, CLAUDE.md); modules with no code yet hold a README naming their FR and planned contents.

The domains array in eslint.config.mjs (14 entries matching the modules/ directory exactly) is the single source that generates the per-module data/-privacy zones — adding a new module requires adding it there or that module's data/ is not made private to other modules.

Mappers are unit-tested in tests/unit/ against the real generated contract: batches.test.ts derives the module-private join-row fixture shape via Parameters<typeof mapBatchRow>[0] instead of duplicating it, and the tests/ directory sits outside the lint zones so test files may import database.types directly, even though app code may not; real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding.

After any migration, database.types.ts must be regenerated and then affected mappers and domain types updated; migrations are additive and supabase/migrations/20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is the canonical schema + RLS migration.

The 'no row means missing' document backfill is a data-layer decision (batches.ts and documents.ts seed every catalog requirement with MISSING_DOC, then overlay submitted rows), and a key still absent after backfill means untracked — to be read via modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts, never by indexing the map directly.

modules/batches/data/metrics.ts's getDashboardMetrics takes the requirement catalog (criticalDocumentKeys) as a parameter rather than importing it, because no single flat catalog exists — the live program_document_requirements table is scoped per scholarship program, so hardcoding one would make the function correct for only one program at a time.

derive-layer sentinels protect downstream math: daysUntil returns Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY for a missing or unparseable date (the 'no known deadline' sentinel that sorts last and never triggers urgency tiers, since NaN would silently corrupt sorting and urgency math), toDisplayDate returns '' for null/unparseable input, and the dashboard's KPI grid renders 'no deadline set' rather than printing the Infinity sentinel as copy.

selectBatchesForDisplay(snapshot) takes only the snapshot and never substitutes mock data: it returns live rows only when ok — authoritative even when ok carries zero rows, per ADR-005 decision 5 — and returns [] for unconfigured or sync-failed; the unit tests pin all four cases.

getBatchesSnapshot is wrapped in react's cache() so app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx and the nested dashboard page share one Supabase query per request — both call it independently for the same request (the layout feeds the MetricsRow, the page the dashboard body).

A guard-clause ordering that checks 'empty' before 'sync-failed' silently swallows the banner whenever a failure yields zero rows — a real sync failure produces zero batches with no fallback, reading as an empty tenant — so RULES 3.19 calls out the ordering explicitly, and the dashboard and billing pages check syncFailed && batches.length === 0 before the empty guard.
